extraction.name: FLEURS: Few-shot Learning Evaluation of Universal Representations of Speech
extraction.description: FLEURS is an n-way parallel speech dataset in 102 languages built on top of the machine translation FLoRes-101 benchmark, with approximately 12 hours of speech supervision per language. It can be used for Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR), Speech Language Identification, Translation and Retrieval tasks.
extraction.creator: Alexis Conneau, Min Ma, Simran Khanuja, Yu Zhang, Vera Axelrod, Siddharth Dalmia, Jason Riesa, Clara Rivera, Ankur Bapna (Meta AI Research, Google Research, Carnegie Mellon University)
extraction.inLanguage: 102 languages including afr, amh, ara, hye, asm, ast, azj, bel, ben, bos, bul, mya, yue, cat, ceb, hrv, ces, dan, nld, eng, est, tgl, fin, fra, ful, glg, lug, kat, deu, ell, guj, hau, heb, hin, hun, isl, ibo, ind, gle, ita, jpn, jav, kea, kam, kan, kaz, khm, kor, kir, lao, lav, lin, lit, luo, ltz, mkd, msa, mal, mlt, cmn, mri, mar, mon, npi, nso, nob, nya, oci, ory, orm, pus, fas, pol, por, pan, ron, rus, srp, sna, snd, slk, slv, som, ckb, spa, swh, swe, tgk, tam, tel, tha, tur, ukr, umb, urd, uzb, vie, cym, wol, xho, yor, zul
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data collection started from the FLoRes-101 dataset. For each sentence in 102 languages, three recordings were collected from three different native speakers, with a sex ratio balance of at least 30/70% when possible. Each recording was then evaluated by additional workers to assess whether it corresponds to the input sentence. Invalid recordings were discarded.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: About 21.5% of the sentences are missing in the first version of the dataset because none of the three recordings were validated.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data is based on the FLoRes-101 dataset, which contains 3001 sentences extracted from English Wikipedia translated into 101 languages by human translators. Only the dev and devtest sets (2009 sentences) were used since the test set is not publicly available.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Text preprocessing includes NFC and FST normalization, lower-casing, normalization and removal of punctuations, and splitting words into characters. Three versions of each sentence are provided: original raw transcript (SRC_RAW), preprocessed version (SRC_NORM), and character-based version (SRC_CHAR). All recordings are kept as-is without data augmentations. Speech sampling rate is 16kHz. Data is split into train, dev and test sets with disjoint speakers between train/dev and test, with a target ratio of 7:1:2.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Each recording was evaluated by additional workers to assess whether the recording corresponds to the input sentence. Invalid recordings were discarded. Source transcripts were reused from human translators from FLoRes-101.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Native speakers of each language, with a sex ratio balance of at least 30/70% when possible.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors plan to fill gaps in future versions of the dataset where sentences are missing due to invalid recordings.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The goal of FLEURS is to enable speech technology in more languages and catalyze research in low-resource speech understanding, with the hope of building speech technologies for everyone.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Results are much better on the Western European group than on other groups like Sub-Saharan African or South Asian, which can be explained in part due to the larger amounts of unlabeled data in WE languages. Reducing the gaps across geographical groups is an important research direction.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: About 21.5% of sentences are missing in the first version because none of the three recordings were validated. The dataset covers read speech from Wikipedia domain only, which may limit generalizability to spontaneous speech or other domains.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: FLEURS is well-suited for several downstream tasks including ASR, Speech-to-Text and Speech-to-Speech Translation, Speech LangID, and Multilingual Speech-to-Speech and Speech-to-Text Retrieval. It is especially suited to evaluate data-efficient multilingual pre-trained representations of speech.

name.evidence: We introduce FLEURS, the Few-shot Learning Evaluation of Universal Representations of Speech benchmark.

description.evidence: FLEURS is an n-way parallel speech dataset in 102 languages built on top of the machine translation FLoRes-101 benchmark, with approximately 12 hours of speech supervision per language. FLEURS can be used for a variety of speech tasks, including Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR), Speech Language Identification (Speech LangID), Translation and Retrieval.

Reducing the gaps across geographical groups is an important research direction for future work.
